title: An in vitro method to evaluate hemolysis of human red blood cells (RBCs) treated by airborne particulate matter (PM10)
author: Mesdaghinia, Pourpak, et al.

steps.title: Prepare PM10 suspension
steps.instruction: Collect PM10 using a high‑volume sampler (flow rate 1.3–1.7 m³/min, Grasebey, USA) onto an 8 × 10 in. fiberglass filter (grade G 653, Whatman, USA). Extract the dried particles by the dry ultrasonic method as previously described, then suspend them in phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS, Biosera, France) to obtain six concentrations: 50, 100, 150, 200, 250, and 300 µg/mL.

steps.title: Prepare blood sample
steps.instruction: Draw whole blood from three donors aged 16–18 years into syringes containing heparin as anticoagulant. Include only donors who are healthy, nonsmoking (≥6 months), not on regular medication, free of inflammation for at least one week, and without occupational exposure to pollutants. Pool equal volumes of the collected blood and dilute the pool ten‑fold with PBS; use this diluted blood for all subsequent assays.

steps.title: Conduct hemolysis assay
steps.instruction: Perform the hemolysis test, which includes preparation of standards and controls, treatment of the diluted blood samples with the PM10 suspensions, measurement of hemoglobin concentration, and calculation of the percent hemolysis.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of results
steps.instruction: Analyze the effect of the six PM10 concentrations on hemolysis percent using R software version 3.4.3. Apply one‑way ANOVA followed by Tukey post‑hoc test; consider results significant when p < 0.05.

description: Current study was done in the stages as follows: sampling and preparation of PM10 suspension and hemolysis test including preparation of standards and controls, preparation of blood, blood sample treatment, and measurement of hemoglobin concentration and calculation of hemolysis percent.
